findings.evidence: Mathlib `LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/Basic.lean:114`: `theorem neg_apply (x y : M₁) : (-B₁) x y = -B₁ x y`; diagonal-evaluation convention marks the repeat, `Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Defs.lean:304`: `theorem inner_sub_sub_self (x y : F) : ⟪x - y, x - y⟫ = …`. Grep shows no EpsilonEridani type among the lemma's arguments (`theorem neg_apply_smul_sub (g : Bilin V) (u v : V) (z : ℝ)`).
findings.fix: Move it to the `LinearMap.BilinForm` namespace and mark the repeated argument, e.g. state `g (z • u - v) (z • u - v) = …` as `LinearMap.BilinForm.apply_smul_sub_self` (keeping the negated form is fine, but then avoid the `neg_apply` prefix), and update the two uses in `Radiative.lean:371,501`.
findings.issue: `neg_apply_smul_sub` is a general `LinearMap.BilinForm` identity (no DIS content; all arguments are Mathlib types) named against upstream usage: in Mathlib `neg_apply` on a bilinear form means applying the *negated form*, not negating the scalar result, and the name omits that both slots carry the same vector, so it reads as `(-g) (z•u) (sub …)` rather than `-g (z•u-v) (z•u-v)`. It is also in the `EpsilonEridani…Kinematics` namespace although its first (and only non-vector/scalar) explicit argument is `g : Bilin V = LinearMap.BilinForm ℝ V`, so `g.neg_apply_smul_sub` does not elaborate and it cannot be upstreamed without renaming.

findings.evidence: AccessMethods.lean:188 `ofTransfer_x_eq … = (ofTransfer …).Q2 / (2 * g p k * (ofTransfer …).y)`; 235 `sigmaMethod_x_eq_div` same shape; 256 `mixedMethod_x_eq` same shape; 248 `sigmaMethod_x_eq … = (electronMethod …).Q2 * (g p (pX - p) + g p kPrime) / (2 * g p k * g p (pX - p))`; 272 `theorem ElectronMethodData.electronMethod_eq … : electronMethod g k p kPrime = ⟨d.xBjElectron M, d.q2Electron, d.yElectron⟩`.
findings.fix: Use one suffix for the `Q² / (2 (p·k) y)` form across the three lemmas (e.g. `ofTransfer_x_eq_Q2_div`, `sigmaMethod_x_eq_Q2_div`, `mixedMethod_x_eq_Q2_div`), give the momentum-level pair a distinguishing suffix instead of bare `_eq`, and rename `ElectronMethodData.electronMethod_eq` to name its right-hand side as its neighbours do (e.g. `electronMethod_eq_xBjElectron_q2Electron_yElectron`).
findings.issue: The bare `_eq` suffix names three different statement shapes in the same section. `ofTransfer_x_eq` (188), `sigmaMethod_x_eq_div` (235) and `mixedMethod_x_eq` (256) have the *same* conclusion `x = Q² / (2 (p·k) y)` under three different names, while `sigmaMethod_x_eq` (248) and `sigmaMethod_y_eq` (242) denote something else (the momentum-level formula). A consumer reading `mixedMethod_x_eq` by analogy with `sigmaMethod_x_eq` gets a different statement. `ElectronMethodData.electronMethod_eq` (272) has the same defect next to neighbours that do spell their right-hand side (`ofTransfer_eq_xBj_Q2_yInel` 183, `electronMethod_eq_xBj_Q2_yInel` 264), and its dot-notation form `d.electronMethod_eq` advertises `d` as the subject when the conclusion's subject is `electronMethod g k p kPrime`.

summary: Names in the new radiative module match their conclusions and no notation is introduced, but the general bilinear-form lemma `neg_apply_smul_sub` is both named against upstream `BilinForm.neg_apply` semantics and filed outside the type's namespace, and the `_eq` suffix is used inconsistently across the parallel reconstruction lemmas in AccessMethods.lean.
